elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase-amount commitment.
elements.evidence: Section 2.1 expressly states that Customer has no minimum purchase commitment.
Section 2.1 expressly states that Customer has no volume commitment.
Section 2.1 expressly states that Customer has no take-or-pay commitment.

elements.element: Customer is required to pay only for actual usage or Services ordered through an Order Form.
elements.evidence: Section 7.1 limits Customer's payment obligation to Fees stated in an Order Form, permits usage-based pricing where expressly provided, and prohibits unidentified platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charges.

elements.element: Any minimum commitment applies only to the current term.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: §2.1 eliminates every minimum purchase, volume, and take-or-pay commitment, so no commitment applies during the current or any later term.

elements.element: Any minimum commitment has a duration of no more than 12 months.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because §2.1 provides that Customer has no minimum commitment at all.

elements.element: Customer may reduce any minimum commitment.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because §2.1 eliminates the commitment that would otherwise require a reduction right.

elements.element: Customer may exercise any commitment-reduction right on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because §2.1 leaves no commitment requiring notice to reduce.

elements.element: Any reconciliation of a commitment shortfall is accomplished through a true-up.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: without a minimum commitment under §2.1, there can be no commitment shortfall requiring reconciliation.

elements.element: No penalty applies for reducing or failing to meet a minimum commitment.
elements.evidence: Section 2.1 eliminates the commitment and therefore eliminates any failure or reduction to which a penalty could attach.

result.reason: The operative redline directly replaces the three-year, non-reducible take-or-pay obligation with an express prohibition on minimum purchase, volume, and take-or-pay commitments. Section 7.1 continues to confine charges to Order Form fees or expressly specified usage pricing. The fallback protections are also satisfied because their predicate—a minimum commitment—is expressly absent. The edit is narrowly confined to §2.1, leaves unrelated commercial terms intact, and is consistent with §12.3. However, drafting quality is poor because Section 7.1 still contemplates that an Order Form may identify a minimum-use charge, creating avoidable ambiguity with the blanket prohibition in §2.1.
